headline: 6 PulseX V1 candidate contracts catalogued on Pulse from unofficial docs and the official FAQ; none verified on an explorer.

findings.text: No PulseChain explorer page could be read. The ipfs.scan.pulsechain.com address page fetched, but it returned only a JavaScript shell with no contract data. A direct scan.pulsechain.com fetch was rejected by the allowlist. Zero addresses were surfaced from explorer name tags.

No official deployed-contracts page was found. app.pulsex.com is only a list of frontend links. The official pulsex.com/faq lists the PLSX and INC token addresses. The third-party, unofficial hexikani PulseChain docs list the v1 router, factory, MasterChef, WPLS and the two tokens.
No audit links were pinned, and no audit PDFs were found or opened.

No GitHub repo is recorded for the protocol, so no deployment artifacts could be walked. A search surfaced a third-party repo (DavidKirkham/bagswap) that repeats the V1 router and factory, but a fetch of that repo failed. It is recorded in unknowns only.
There is one chain, Pulse (chainId 369). It is not in the DeFiPunkd read-API supported chain list, so no surfacer or read-API call is possible for these addresses.
No factory enumeration was possible. The V1 factory 0x1715a3E4A142d8b698131108995174F37aEBA10D is on an unsupported chain for the read API. No child pairs were recorded.
Roles were assigned from the vocabulary: router, factory, token, and other (MasterChef, WPLS). All are tentative, with actor_class unknown because no bytecode was read.
Every address in admin_addresses traces to a fetched URL in evidence[]. Snippet-only sightings and the unfetched BagSwap and Rubic-derived claims are in unknowns[] only.

rationale.verdict: Discovery found 6 V1 candidates plus 2 V2 neighbours on Pulse from an unofficial docs page and the official FAQ. No explorer, GitHub or audit source could be read, so the grade is unknown.

evidence.shows: Protocol website probe succeeded. The page is only a list of links to ways to run PulseX frontend code, with no contract addresses. It is the frontend entry point.

Official PulseX site FAQ. It lists the PLSX token address 0x95B303987A60C71504D99Aa1b13B4DA07b0790ab and the INC (Incentive) token address 0x2fa878Ab3F87CC1C9737Fc071108F904c0B0C95d, linked to the PulseChain explorer. Its meta-description calls PulseX a Uniswap fork with PLSX Liquidity Provider incentivization.

Unofficial third-party PulseChain docs, listed as a candidate source only. Under Mainnet PulseX v1 they list PulseXRouter02 0x98bf93ebf5c380C0e6Ae8e192A7e2AE08edAcc02, PulseXFactory02 0x1715a3E4A142d8b698131108995174F37aEBA10D, MasterChef 0xB2Ca4A66d3e57a5a9A12043B6bAD28249fE302d4, Wrapped PLS 0xA1077a294dDE1B09bB078844df40758a5D0f9a27, and the PLSX and INC tokens. They state that v1 has a liquidity-provider fee-calculation bug and was replaced by v2. Under Mainnet PulseX v2 they list router 0x165C3410fC91EF562C50559f7d2289fEbed552d9 and factory 0x29eA7545DEf87022BAdc76323F373EA1e707C523.

Third-party Rubic SDK docs. They give the same address, 0x98bf93ebf5c380C0e6Ae8e192A7e2AE08edAcc02, as the PulseX V1 contract address. This is independent corroboration of the V1 router address, but it is not an explorer source.

Explorer probe for the PLSX token page linked from the official FAQ. The fetch returned only a 'You need to enable JavaScript' shell, so no on-chain content was readable. It is recorded as a failed on-chain probe.

unknowns: D1-offchain: PulseChain explorer fetch for the PLSX token (ipfs.scan.pulsechain.com) returned a JS-only shell. A direct fetch of scan.pulsechain.com/address/0x98bf93eb... was rejected by the allowlist. No name-tag search could be performed, and no explorer-verified role or bytecode exists for any address.

D1: Pulse (chainId 369) is not in the DeFiPunkd read-API supported chain list. No /api/contract/read or /api/safe/owners calls are possible, so owner, admin and timelock state for the router, factory and MasterChef are unread.

D2: No official PulseX deployed-contracts page was found. app.pulsex.com, pulsex.com/faq and the pulsex.com site were checked, and a pulsex.com root fetch was rejected by the allowlist. deployed_contracts_doc is left null because the only full address list is the unofficial hexikani doc.
D3: No audit links were pinned and none were discovered, so there are no audit-era addresses.

D4: protocol.github is empty and no official GitHub repo was discovered. A search surfaced github.com/DavidKirkham/bagswap, which claims the V1 router and factory and a V1 init hash 0x59fffffddd756cba9095128e53f3291a6ba38b21e3df744936e7289326555d62 and a 'documented fee bug on V1'. Fetching that repo failed, so this is snippet-only and not cited.

D5: chain Pulse: only unofficial third-party docs (hexikani, Rubic SDK) and the official FAQ (tokens only) surfaced addresses. The V1 router and factory are not confirmed by any official source or explorer.

D6: The V1 factory's allPairs / getPair enumeration could not be read (unsupported chain, explorer unreadable). A snippet of the BagSwap PR claims about 65k V1 pairs, which is unverified. If a read becomes possible, apply the 50-child cap per factory.

D8: Snippet-only sighting, not in admin_addresses. Search snippets show that on Ethereum, address 0x1715a3E4A142d8b698131108995174F37aEBA10D is labelled 'PulseChain: Omnibridge Proxy'. This is the same hex as the claimed PulseX V1 factory on Pulse. Do not conflate the two chains.
D8: Snippet-only sighting of the PulseX V2 sample pair WPLS/PLSX 0x149b2c629e652f2e89e11cd57e5d4d77ee166f9f, from BagSwap. It was not fetched, so it is not recorded.

D7: Role for MasterChef 0xB2Ca4A66... is tentative ('other'). The hexikani page lists the same MasterChef under both v1 and v2, and it is unverified whether it is still active or has V1-specific admin rights.

D2: No governance forum, bug bounty, security contact or docs site was found. The app.pulsex.com and pulsex.com pages show only a Telegram chat and Twitter, so these protocol_metadata fields are null.

protocol_metadata.about: PulseX is a Uniswap V2-style automated market maker on PulseChain where users swap PRC20 tokens and provide liquidity to constant-product pairs. Its official site describes it as a Uniswap fork with PLSX liquidity-provider incentivization. Unofficial docs say the V1 deployment has a bug in liquidity-provider fee calculation and was superseded by a V2 deployment.
